REFUTED_BEFORE: matches G-06 via 'cascade' — Cluster / cascade filter (isolated pumps better) (Live isolated 65% vs cascade 38% (p=.047 on 7d). Honest 249d: 56.1% vs 57.1% — and 11+ clusters were actually best.)

history: This project has already run this experiment twice under different names. G-10 (re-pump recency) tested exactly the population dedup_hours=24 would remove: a coin that fired 6-48h ago. The live signal at p=.066 went flat at p=.58 on honest data. A 24h cap is precisely a rule that deletes those 6-48h repeat fills, so G-10 says the deleted trades are statistically indistinguishable from the ones kept — dropping them cannot move net EV per trade, it only shrinks n. G-06 (cluster/cascade filter) is the same causal claim one level up: 'one distribution campaign should contribute one trade, not several correlated ones' IS 'isolated pumps beat cascades'. Honest 249d gave 56.1% isolated vs 57.1% cascade, and 11+ clusters were the BEST bucket — the correlation the proposal calls harmful was measured and found mildly beneficial. G-14 adds the third strike: split-half WR correlation by coin r = -0.002, so same-name stacking carries no persistent penalty to remove. The proposal's own framing concedes the weak form of this: it argues 24h over 48h purely on sample preservation, i.e. it is optimising power for an effect whose existence was already refuted at p=.58. The 0.12% slippage haircut is charged per extra fill on both sides of the comparison and does not create a per-trade EV lift from deletion; a filter that removes average-EV trades is a volume dial, the same trap as G-08. Blocking terms 're-pump', 'recent pump same coin', 'cluster filter', 'isolated pump' all fire.; mechanism: The mechanism is not a reason, it is a re-description of a pattern already refuted. Dedup is already ON at dedup_hours=6, and detection uses pump_window_h<=6, so 'one campaign contributes one trade' is satisfied by the incumbent. The only population 6->24 actually removes is the second fill in a coin that pumped again 6-24h later — which is exactly G-10 (re-pump recency, 6-48h band), where a live p=.066 went flat at p=.58 on honest data, and adjacent to G-06 where isolated-vs-cascade collapsed to 56.1% vs 57.1% with 11+ clusters best. The proposal offers no reason those second fills are worse trades; 'correlated' is a variance/portfolio property, not a per-trade EV property, so the stated cause cannot produce the predicted move in EV or WR. It equally predicts the opposite: a coin re-pumping into an already-stretched move is a higher short entry, and G-26 found uptrend pumps short BETTER, so removing the second leg should lower per-trade EV. The one channel that does move the number is accounting, not edge — deleting the fills that pay the 0.12% extra-fill haircut raises mean EV/trade while cutting total PnL, the same volume-for-a-dial trade that killed G-08 (ACC/XC). The 24h boundary is set by convenience ('calendar-day'), not by any measured campaign life in this context; hold-12h implies a 12h trade life, so 24h is unmotivated. The falsification clause references a '48h cap' arm that does not exist in the arena, making the stated test unfalsifiable as written, and the class label 'universe' is wrong — dedup_hours changes no coin's eligibility, it is a timing/entry_trigger dial.; statistics: The proposal's own framing concedes it is a sample-preserving variant, which means the trades it actually changes are only the repeat fills inside a 24h window — a small subset of the shared detection stream, so the arm's screen population will be nearly identical to control (screen_n=1534, screen_wr=49.739, screen_ev=0.016) and the delta it can register is correspondingly tiny. The context supplies no count of within-24h repeat detections, so there is no number here establishing that the changed-trade subset is large enough to move EV at all; by the stated rule that a fixed n=100 detects only very large effects and small ideas need the full planned n=600, an effect concentrated in a thin slice of fills cannot clear corrected alpha 0.00833. Worse, that slice is structurally confounded: repeat fills within a day cluster in whichever few coins pumped repeatedly and in whatever regime the 60.7-day window happened to contain (176 coins, 246445 candles, live tier only n=19), which is precisely the PM/SN/MT pattern that killed G-10 re-pump recency (live p=.066 to flat p=.58) and G-14 coin persistence (r=-0.002). The hypothesis is also unfalsifiable as written — it pre-commits to reinterpreting a null as evidence about the 48h arm, which is max-of-k reasoning across two correlated dedup arms against a lifetime budget already at 6 tests. Finally, the EV case rests on saving the 0.12% haircut on extra fills, but removing fills also removes their wins, and no number in this context shows repeat fills are worse than first fills.
